channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Saints LS Zach Wood suffered a calf strain and is expected to miss four-to-six weeks.
item.description: Wood felt calf tightness on Wednesday and was diagnosed with a Grade II calf strain after undergoing tests. The 33-year-old has not missed a game since signing with the Saints in 2017 but is now expected to be out for at least four weeks.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Cardinals TE Trey McBride (rest/back) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: No need to panic after McBride was seen working off to the side Wednesday; the Cardinals listed him as DNP with a rest/back designation. Despite the back being added to the designation, it does not seem like a serious injury worry with the Cardinals also giving him the “resting player” tag. This reads as a rest day for McBride, he is still good to go for Week 2 against the Seahawks.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle/hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Emmanwori is still unable to get in a full practice as he nurses a pesky ankle injury, also adding a hip issue to his practice designation. He will likely need a full practice before he is set to return for the Seahawks. Fellow safety Ty Okada (hamstring) missed practice on Wednesday; both players missed Week 1 and are in jeopardy of missing Week 2 against the Cardinals.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Kupp popped up on the injury report with a back issue, though he was listed as a limited participant. The veteran 33-year-old may just be having his practice reps managed as he deals with a back ailment. Barring a change, Kupp is still trending to play Week 2 against the Cardinals.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Seahawks WR Tory Horton (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Horton missed Week 1, dealing with a hamstring injury from training camp. He now finally gets in a full practice, opening Week 2 with a full participation designation. The Seahawks are preparing for the 23-year-old to return against the Cardinals, though Horton is best left off fantasy rosters with Drew Lock the starting quarterback for now.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Malik Willis (toe) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Willis popped up on the Dolphins’ injury report with a toe injury, though he was a full practice participant. This indicates the issue is minor enough for the 27-year-old to keep practicing at full strength. Note down Willis’ toe issue, but expect him to be back out there for Week 2 against the 49ers.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Dolphins EDGE Chop Robinson (concussion protocol) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Robinson appeared in Week 1 against the Raiders and is now in concussion protocol to open up Week 2. The 23-year-old has a history of concussions, entering the protocol twice last season. Robinson will be thoroughly evaluated before he officially returns, given this is his third head injury over the last calendar year.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Coker was wearing a boot after rolling his left ankle in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss against the Bears. Head coach Dave Canales told reporters that the team is confident in ramping him up in practice. The 24-year-old got in a limited practice Wednesday, doing an “extended warm up” on the side and getting a “couple of snaps” on things the Panthers are looking for him to execute. Canales added the “hope is to ramp that up a little bit more tomorrow and then cut them loose Friday. So I expect him to play on Sunday.” Coker’s ankle injury is certainly something to keep an eye on, but Canales and the Panthers are confident he will play in Week 2 against the Falcons.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: 49ers K Eddy Pineiro (illness) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Pineiro was a non-participant in practice due to an illness. It’s still early in the week, so the 31-year-old kicker will likely return in time for Week 2 against the Dolphins.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Kittle also started out last week as limited, so this seems to be regular practice management for the veteran. He appeared in Week 1 and was targeted five times. Expect Kittle to be back out there for Week 2 against the Dolphins, barring any setbacks.-Aditya Fuldeore
